tracks.title: 燒豆腐 Sio tāu-hū
tracks.subject: A stone-mill tofu maker grinds beans from 3 a.m. and leaves the first warm block wrapped in cloth on a quiet woman's windowsill; each day she returns the cloth folded square, and finally a note.

tracks.title: 漏氣 Làu-khuì
tracks.genre: Taigi smoky torch-song jazz with muted trumpet
tracks.subject: A woman who runs a bicycle-repair shop beside a temple dips the same customer's back-tyre tube in the water basin every Tuesday and realises the single pinhole is made by his own pin; she patches it slowly anyway.

tracks.title: 手尺麵線 Tshiú-tshioh mī-suànn
tracks.genre: Taigi 1970s dance-hall twist pop with horn riffs
tracks.subject: A mee-sua noodle maker measures every bundle by his own outstretched arms until his new wife, whose arms are shorter, makes shorter bundles, and the customers start queuing for hers because the short strands cook faster.

tracks.title: 菜瓜衫 Tshài-kue-sann
tracks.genre: Taigi Appalachian-style old-time clawhammer banjo folk
tracks.subject: A grandmother sews a little bag from each grandchild's outgrown shirt to cover every young loofah on her trellis against fruit flies, so the garden ends up wearing the whole family.

tracks.title: 賰三秒 Tshun sann-bió
tracks.subject: A woman who always steps off the kerb with exactly three seconds left on the pedestrian green-man countdown mistimes it once, and the man waiting at the corner holds up his hand to stop a scooter for her.

tracks.title: 十二聲 Tsap-jī siann
tracks.subject: A Tamsui church bell-ringer who must pull exactly twelve strokes at noon loses count every day because the florist across the street waves from her window, so the congregation files out for lunch two strokes early.

tracks.title: 骨牌少一塊 Kut-pâi tsió tsit-tè
tracks.genre: Taigi 1990s Hokkien power ballad with sax solo
tracks.subject: Four old friends play 32-tile tin-gau domino at a Lukang temple courtyard table and have used a bottle cap for the missing tile for twenty years, until the carpenter among them carves a replacement from an ebony chopstick.

tracks.title: 倒寫的名 Tò-siá ê miâ
tracks.subject: A seal-carver's apprentice must carve his girlfriend Huē-bûn's name in mirror writing and has ruined ninety-nine stones, so on the hundredth he presses it first on his own palm.

tracks.title: 媒人喙糊瘰瘰 Muê-lâng-tshuì hôo-lui-lui
tracks.subject: A village matchmaker tells the groom's family that the girl eats very little and the girl's family that the boy hardly talks, then at the first meeting he talks nonstop and she eats nonstop and they suit perfectly.

tracks.title: 旋轉門 Suān-tsuân-mn̂g
tracks.subject: A white-gloved hotel doorman in Taipei counts one-two-three for every turn of the revolving door, and a woman in a green skirt who takes it twice every Thursday afternoon never says why.

tracks.title: 三〇七號房 Sann-lîng-tshit hō-pâng
tracks.subject: A day-shift hotel receptionist in Taichung has quietly kept room 307 for a regular Tuesday salesman for a year, writes his name in the register, and finally decides to give him hers.

tracks.title: 字模盤 Jī-bôo-puânn
tracks.subject: In 1985 a Tainan trading-company typist, working a Chinese typewriter with a 2,500-character tray, keeps slipping her boyfriend's character into the contracts, until he turns up and mistypes the word for love.

tracks.title: 紙條仔的字 Tsuá-tiâu-á ê jī
tracks.genre: Taigi West Coast cool-jazz chamber ballad
tracks.subject: A Taipei taxi driver keeps a tin box of the scrap-paper addresses passengers scribbled, reads each handwriting like a face, and one night a young man hands him a slip that only says take me home.

tracks.title: 粉筆寫的聖詩 Hún-pit siá ê sèng-si
tracks.genre: Taigi Presbyterian four-part hymn with pump organ
tracks.subject: A fourteen-year-old who letters the hymn numbers on the chalkboard in a Tainan Presbyterian church smudges a 3 into an 8 one Sunday, so half the congregation sings two different hymns at once.

tracks.title: 皮箱的貼紙 Phuê-siunn ê thiap-tsóa
tracks.subject: A young bellboy at a Sun Moon Lake hotel guesses each guest's hometown from the stickers on their suitcase, until a woman's first sticker turns out to be his own village railway station.
